J U D G M E N T :
 1.0

Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of the state's appeal challenging the order dated 27.03.2018 ("the impugned order" in short) of Ld. Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate (Central)
("ADM" in short), New Delhi whereby, the application under Rule 3.1.1(3) of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011("FSSR" in short) filed by FSO was dismissed observing that the respondents deserve benefit of doubt in view of contradictory reports of Food Analyst and of Central Food Laboratory(CFL).
2.0

Briefly stating, the facts as per appeal are that :
(i) on 29.12.2014, Food Safety Officer ("FSO" in short), purchased sample of "Pasteurized Full Cream Milk" from Sh. Satish Sharma/respondent no.1.
The sample consisted of approx. 2 x 1 litre taken from sealed poly pack (ready for sale), bearing label declaration "Pasteurized Full Cream Milk" on it;

(ii) the sample of Pasteurized Full Cream Milk was taken after proper mixing with the help of clean & dry measure by rotating in all possible directions i.e. up & Food Safety Officer vs Sh.Satish Sharma & Ors.

The sample of pasteurized full cream milk was divided into four equal parts then and there by putting into four clean and dry glass bottles and 40 drops of formalin was added in each bottle with the help of clean and dry dropper.

Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to the provisions of FSS Act and Rules/
Regulations framed thereunder;
(iii) one counterpart of the sample under sealed cover was sent to Food Analyst.
Other two counterparts were deposited with Designated Officer.
As the FBO did not make a request to send the fourth counter part for analysis from NABL Acreedited Laboratory, the fourth sealed counterpart was also deposited with the Designated Officer;

(iv) the Food Analyst vide his report dated 12.01.2015 opined "The sample is substandard because milk solids not fat is less than the prescribed minimum limit of 9.0%;

if so desired.
An appeal against Food Analyst's report was preferred.

3.0 The appellant /FSO has challenged the impugned order on the grounds that the Ld. ADM failed to appreciate that in terms of the provisions contained in Section 47(c) of FSS Act read with Rule 2.4.6 of FSS Rules, 2011, the report of Referral Food Laboratory is final and has to be given precedence over the report of Food Analyst; and that the Ld. ADM even failed to appreciate the law as laid by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Delhi Administration Vs. Vidya Gupta [Crl. Appeal No.
625/18].

sentences.text: 4.0 The respondents have sought dismissal of the appeal pleading that the Ld. ADM rightly acquitted the respondents giving benefit of doubt to them in view of variation in Reports of Food Analyst and Referral Food Laboratory.
4.1 Ld. counsel for the respondents also argued that in case this court is inclined to set aside the impugned order, they would Food Safety Officer vs Sh.Satish Sharma & Ors.

like to point out that the Ld. ADM failed to record any findings on other contentions raised by them before him vide their reply, including their request for cross examination of FSO.

4.2 Ld. Counsel for the respondents no. 4 & 5 also argued that the Ld. ADM did not refer to any of their contentions viz. the procedure adopted by RFL (IS:1224,1977) for arriving at the fat content in the milk was gerber method and was not proper, as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
Further, even addition of excess preservative/ 40 drops of formalin rendered the milk sub standard.

5.0 Let me at the outset refer to the impugned order, the relevant portion of which reads as under:
"

and Milk Solids not fat 9.3% (prescribed standards not less than 9.0%).
He cited judgments namely FSO Vs. Abdul Jameel, Crl. L.P. No. 2 of 2014 decided on 3.1.2014 by Delhi High Court, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has given benefit of doubt to the accused persons.

He also raised point that FSO should have put 16/18 drops of formalin (preservative), but in present case FSO has added 40 drops of formalin in each bottle and with the result the milk became substandard due to excess quantity of preservative as held by the Hon'ble Kerala High Court in matter titled K R Gopinathan Nair, FI Vs. T N. Ittyavirah and another in Crl. Appeal No. 174 of 1972,
decided on 5.10.1972.

sentences.text: The matter was kept reserved for orders on 26.3.2018.

I am convinced with the Ld. Counsel that since the two expert reports were contradictory to each other, while the Food Analyst adjudged deficiency of the sample was milk solids not fat and on the other side the Referral Food Laboratory reported deficiency of milk Food Safety Officer vs Sh.Satish Sharma & Ors.
:: 9 ::
fat.
I am of the opinion that the benefit of doubt should rightly be given to the respondents.

From the above said facts and circumstances and documents placed on record, it is not proved that the Food Business Operator/ Respondent has committed offence of selling substandard "Pasteurized Full Cream Milk" in violation of Section 26(2)(ii) &
27(1) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 read with Section 3(1)(zx) of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
ORDER:

(i) After taking into consideration of all the facts and circumstances of the case and material available on record, I did not find it a fit case to impose penalty in terms of Rule 3.1.2(1) of Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 and, therefore, to meet the ends of justice, I dismiss the application filed by the FSO.

(ii) in terms of provisions of Rule 3.1.2(5) of Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011.
let copy of this order be served to FBO and Food Safety Officer.

(RANJEET SINGH) ADJUDICATING OFFICER/ ADM (CENTRAL) Govt. OF NCT OF DELHI"

sentences.text: The said observation was made without referring to any provision of law and recording reasons.
It may be mentioned that Rule 2.4.6 FSS Rules lays down that report of Referral Food Laboratory shall be final.
There is no discussion by the Ld.ADM in this respect.
Not going any further into the purport of this provision and its interpretation by the Higher courts, the matter is remanded back to Ld. ADM.
Ld. ADM is directed to decide the matter afresh after duly considering the contentions raised by both the sides in the light of provision of law.
5.2 Parties are directed to appear before Ld.ADM on 31.05.2019 at 02:00 pm.
6.0 Appeal is disposed of accordingly.
7.0 TCR be returned alongwith copy of this judgment.
8.0 Appeal file be consigned to Record POONAM  Room.
